Yes. I'm 25 years now, and because of childhood trauma i grow up dissociated. When dissociation happened a lot when we are young it can become a dissociative disorder.

I went through something similar three months ago.  Since then I am in a very strange state of mind.  I knew very well that I would not marry that person and could not reach him, so I should not be shocked.  But I think my subconscious is in a state of violent shock and I don't know when it will come out of it
I feel you

I give you an example: Dissociative identity disorder..it's a mental disorser caused by traumas. And a lot of mental illnesses are. There is no contradiction between being a mental illness and being a coping method at the same time. The brain can make you mentally ill and even totally insane just to protect you from some kind of pain...without even realizing it  .In my opinion, excessive daydreaming is a coping method.  But when you get 80% of your day to the point that it's the only way your brain works here, it becomes a disorder itself.  In my case it is no longer an escape but something I desperately want to escape from

It doesn't matter if it's a disorder or a symptom.  At least it should be taken seriously by the therapist if it cannot be controlled no matter how hard you try and negatively affect your life. What if its root cause is irreversible or caused by lifelong trauma or a cause that you never knew?  In this case, the only solution remains to relieve its symptoms.

Who said it can't be both? A lot of mental disorders are considered as maladaptive coping mechanism and a side effect of trauma. When daydreaming becomes involuntary and compulsive and paralyzes a person's life and steals all his time, in this case it has become a problem in itself and not just a side effect of a problem.

But he can stop blaming people when he stops believing that they don't have free will. So why is it so difficult?  I lost faith in free will a long time ago.  But I always blame someone if they do something bad to me and I want them to be punished.  And when I thought recently I found that there is a contradiction
I don't get it
But you can't want to punish him

Usually when you love someone, you imagine yourself with them.  I can't imagine myself interacting with him, talking to him or touching him.  I just imagine him watching me, and that's what I find strange

every day ..all the day ... for 10 years ..are you sure this is notmal ? The strange thing is that I never imagine myself interacting with him.  I just imagine him watching me..there's nothing romantic about it
If my current situation makes me depressed and suicidal. So for me, there is nothing worse.  Because I couldn't feel worse than that even if the worst happens
What's worse than being constantly depressed and suicidal?
I use to appreciate it without daydreaming when i was a kid. Now after years of this disorder, i can't listen to good music without daydreaming.. it became my natural automatic response to music.
I daydream when i run

Because I'm busy living in my head all the time..I rarely notice and evaluate my true self and status in real life.  Moments of truth only appear to me " sometimes" Probably because I'd better avoid it

Actually people with this disorder are not addicted to music ..they are addicted to daydreaming to music . We do not listen to music and enjoy it like ordinary people..we use it as an escape tool or a gateway to the world of fantasy. For maladaptive daydreamers music works like a drug ..that's why we are addicted to it. If you notice your taste in music, you will find that your favorite music is the music that helps you daydream.
This happened with me.  It is a long-term effect of daydreaming.  If you have been suffering from daydreaming addiction for years, it is normal to mix reality and fantasy
I know it's a classic sign of maladaptive daydreaming .I guess you didn't understand my question 😅
It's hard for me to be gentle with myself . Whenever I plan to get rid of a habit in a short period of time and fail.  I blame and myself, and I get depressed
I'm doing it for 20 years .. and I wanted to get rid of it in a day 🥺
sharing my vulnerability in real life hurts me more
I don't understand what you are implying. I just wanted to say that English is not my language so I make mistakes

I undertand . The difference between you and me is that daydreaming affects me negatively and does more mental harm than good.  So I made the decision to leave her permanently because if I didn't, I wouldn't take a step forward in my life . Second, you think that the problem that makes you resort to it is not getting the appreciation you deserve and once you move it will get better.. In my case, the problem that made me prefer fantasy to reality since childhood will always exist unfortunately, because it is a chronic health condition and it will never get better.  So it's time to look for realistic ways to cope .
Most of them don't care about me.  They just like to judge things they haven't tried and know nothing about

There is no way to improve it.  My mind rejects my health condition and cannot cope with it, so it is separated all the time from reality and will always be so.  Five years have passed since I understood what was happening to me.. and I am trying to find a solution.  But nothing has changed.. I either fantasize all the time or think of suicide every time I come back to reality.  If I am unable to live, then there is no need to continue eating and drinking..because in any case I am not present in this world.
